workout.tip.basis: Each step decides for itself whether it uses power, heart rate or pace: click a step's target to change it (marked "Set"). Steps marked "Auto" follow the session type (easy road runs / long runs use power, with heart rate capped at your easy-run ceiling; trail runs use heart rate; intervals use power). The numbers come from your current CP, LTHR, easy-run ceiling and threshold pace.
workout.tip.chart: The horizontal axis is time ("until lap button" steps are drawn at a fixed width, hatched). Height is a common intensity scale: threshold = 100 (the dashed line) — power ÷ CP, pace as speed ÷ threshold speed, heart rate converted — so the steps of a mixed session can be compared directly. Colour: the hue is the target type (heart rate red, power yellow, pace blue, RPE purple, no target grey), darker = harder (in dark mode brighter = harder). Hover or tap a step to see its own units; click a step to select it below.
workout.tip.tss: Training load (est.) = Σ seconds × intensity² × 100 ÷ 3600, intensity = the target's midpoint on the common scale (threshold = 1). Heart-rate steps: your own relation when you have enough steady runs with power and heart rate, else Friel's run heart-rate and pace zones paired by zone (estimate); steps with no target get a fixed value by type. All estimates; how far running pace load differs from this formula is unverified.
workout.tip.rules: Live checks: zone 5 reps at least 2 min each (a Taiwanese coach); zone 5 rests no longer than the shortest rep and no more than 3 min (Buchheit); zone 3 reps at least 3 min each (Haugen 2022, lower bound); the day's time cap (schedule preferences: a soft cap only warns, a hard cap blocks); errors such as choosing power without a CP. Quality sessions are also compared with this level's standard workout to see whether they count as a step up.
workout.tip.lastRest: No rest after the last rep: go straight into the next step. COROS interval groups can't do this, so the push flattens it into individual steps (one lap each).
workout.tip.watch: COROS watch limits: running power only takes absolute watts (no % CP); one target per step; no ramp steps. Below are the steps that will actually be sent.
workout.tip.tpl: Workouts with a source (author / book / URL under each one), filtered by this session's type. Quality sessions come in three families, judged first by main-set intensity, then by rep length: Aerobic intervals (≤ 101% CP; long tempo 15–30 min per rep, cruise intervals 6–15 min, shorter ones count as cruise too), VO2max intervals (above threshold, 2–5 min per rep, rest about 1:1; short-on/short-off like 30/30 also go here) and Speed (≤ 2 min per rep, rest ≥ 2×, e.g. R, strides, short hill sprints). Trail runs come in three: structured climbing (stairs, steady-grade routes; HR / power ranges set as usual), technical terrain (time + climb + RPE, no HR or power target; RPE ≥ 7 counts as a quality session) and downhill technique / eccentric (time + descent). Each one has a line on its training purpose. Each step uses its source's own target: Palladino / Stryd use power; Friel, Uphill Athlete and Pfitzinger use heart rate; Daniels, Canova and Billat use pace (converted only when the app lacks the source's number, marked as an estimate). Once inserted they are ordinary steps you can edit; an edited quality session is judged as a step up or not by its own reps and intensity. At the top of each family are this session's three "recommended" picks (for quality sessions, #1 = the next step on the interval ladder); the rest are folded below.
workout.tip.total: Total time is the sum of the steps below: to change the time, change the steps (clicking here opens the structure).
workout.tip.pacePct: Pace % is a multiple of your threshold pace: bigger = slower (e.g. 114–129% is Friel zone 2).
workout.tip.rpe: RPE on a 0–10 scale (Foster): 3 moderate, 5 hard, 7 very hard, 10 maximal. On technical terrain and downhills heart rate stays low and power is unreliable, so only RPE and climb / descent count; the watch gets no target for this step, and the RPE and climb go in the step name. A max of 7 or higher makes this a quality session (48 h from other quality sessions). Load is counted from what the watch records.

feas.how_text: "Time to get ready?": your last 4 weeks, a little more each week with an easy week every 4th, up to 3 weeks before the race. "Ready now?": the longest outing and the biggest week you actually did in the last 6 weeks. Both are compared with the race's hardest day. Advice only, your event is never changed; the thresholds are estimates.
feas.how_text_baiyue: "With today's fitness": the summit day's climb and hours (and, with a turnaround time, the climb rate it needs) against your biggest day of the last 6 months (when those were normal training — no break, cutback or injury layoff — further back to just after the latest interruption, at most 24 months); the hardest item counts, in the race calculator's effort words (Easy, Stable, Hard, Max, Over). "Ready now?": how many summit-day simulations you did in the 8 weeks before the trip. Advice only, your event is never changed; the percentage mapping is an estimate.

setup.title: A few basics first
setup.intro: Sex, age and weight calibrate the calculations and only you know them; everything else (thresholds, heat, climbing…) is estimated from your activities. You can change them later in Settings → Personal.
setup.remind: Not now? Press "Later": if anything is still missing, you'll be asked again in {days} days.
setup.sex_why: Sets the default anaerobic capacity and the energy estimates.
setup.age_why: Used for the energy estimates and, until there is a max HR, the climbing HR cap (220 − age, an estimate).
setup.weight_why: Used for power per kilo (W/kg), running effectiveness, the race calculator and the default pack weight.

fitimport.intro: Not syncing from COROS, or filling in old history: upload the FIT files (TCX and GPX too) exported from Garmin, Suunto, Polar, Strava or another platform — several files at once, or a whole folder. The same file is never imported twice, and a run that also came from a sync counts once.

expimport.intro: A sync only reaches back a few months to a year. To fill in older history, export your whole account from the platform (one ZIP file) and upload it here: every FIT, TCX and GPX activity file inside is imported, other files are skipped and listed. The same file is never imported twice, and a run that also came from a sync counts once.
expimport.limits: Up to {gb} GB per ZIP. Keep this page open while it uploads; after that the server processes it in the background and you can leave.
expimport.how.title: How to get an export
expimport.how.garmin: Garmin: in your Garmin account, Data Management › Export Your Data › Request Data Export, then download the ZIP from the e-mail (it can take a few days). Upload the whole ZIP as it is; no need to unpack it.
expimport.how.tp: TrainingPeaks: Settings › Export Data › Workout Files, for a period of 12 months or less. If you get a folder, use "Choose a folder" under Import FIT files above; a ZIP, upload it here.
expimport.how.coros: COROS: sign in to Training Hub on a computer, choose Export Data on the activity list with the FIT format, and download it from the e-mail. A ZIP: upload it here; a set of FIT files: use "Choose a folder".
expimport.how.own: Your own files: put the .fit files (or .tcx, .gpx) in a folder and compress it into a ZIP.
expimport.how.later: Polar's "Download your data" and Apple Health's "Export All Health Data" cannot be imported yet. In Polar Flow on the web you can export each session as FIT or TCX and upload it with Import FIT files.
expimport.background: The server is processing it in the background: you can leave this page and come back for the result.
expimport.unfinished: The last upload did not finish ({got} / {all} MB). Choose the same file again to go on where it stopped.
expimport.interrupted: Processing stopped ({done} / {total} done), perhaps because the server restarted. Press Continue to go on; what is imported is not done again.
expimport.kind.garmin: A Garmin account export: every uploaded activity file inside (FIT, TCX, GPX) is imported; the rest (daily statistics, sleep, profile) is skipped.
expimport.kind.polar: This is a Polar account export: its training sessions are JSON and cannot be imported yet. Export each session as FIT or TCX in Polar Flow on the web and upload them with Import FIT files.
expimport.kind.apple_health: This is an Apple Health export: its route files have no heart rate or sport, so they cannot be imported yet.

fitfolder.title: Auto-import folder (desktop Chrome, Edge)
fitfolder.intro: Choose a folder that holds FIT files (for example where your watch or another platform exports them); every time you open this site, the new files in it are imported. A web page cannot read the folder in the background, so files are imported only when you open the site, and only on this computer and browser.

legend.levels_note:
Walking sessions (steep power hiking, hikes): a hike, a walk or a trail run all count as the right sport.
How intensity is measured: with the session classifier, the higher of Zone 3 time (bar 10 min) and equivalent T@VO2max (bar 4 min); without it, the time at or above threshold (power ≥ 95 % CP or HR ≥ LTHR; bar 10 min, short intervals 60 % of the plan). The 80 %, 50 % and 1.5× bands applied to intensity are estimates; so is counting it partly done when time and training load are on plan (intervals.icu and TrainingPeaks rate completion by load / time).

daysplit.tap_hint: Tap the profile to add where a day ends; drag to adjust; tap a day end to remove it. Near a candidate it snaps to it.

workout.intensity_tip: Numbers are % of threshold (CP / threshold pace / heart rate converted), threshold = 100. Moderate 80–95, high ≥ 95: Palladino's three zones (= Seiler's zone 2 / zone 3). Marathon pace always counts as moderate (Seiler, Daniels' M pace, Pfitzinger). Zone 5 (≥ 106) is part of high.
